summary.name: NotificationNanny
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source macOS menu bar app that moves, resizes and recolours notification banners and can replace the Notification Center panel with a customisable one.
use_cases: Moving macOS notification banners to a different corner or display
Making notification banners larger or smaller
Giving different apps their own notification position, size or colour
Holding banners until the display wakes up
Replacing the default Notification Center panel with a customised one
summary.what_it_does: NotificationNanny lets you place macOS notification banners at any of nine anchor points with fine offsets, with independent settings per display. You can scale banners from 50% to 250%, tint the background or text, pick an animation, or use a custom styled banner that keeps the app's actions and inline replies. Apps can be given their own position, display, size and colour, and organised into named groups. Banners can be auto-dismissed after 1–300 seconds or held until the display wakes. It also provides a custom Notification Center with colours, sizing, app filters and optional real macOS widgets. It uses macOS Accessibility to observe and move notification windows, processing this locally.
notable: Nine anchor points plus fine offsets, with independent settings for each display
Custom banners keep app actions and inline replies working
Custom Notification Center with optional real macOS widgets
caveats: Requires macOS Accessibility permission, which may need to be granted again after an update
Uses private macOS internals, so OS updates can affect its behaviour
Requires macOS 14 or later; widget display needs an extra permission
